Method of Attack: A backdoor planted in the xz/liblzma open source compression tool, which is part of the xz-utils package. The malicious code was distributed via altered release tarballs and activated under certain conditions, modifying the build process and injecting a malicious payload into the source tree. The payload can bypass authentication, possibly allowing unauthorized remote access.
Discoverer: Andres Freund, a Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft and PostgreSQL developer
Impacted Systems: Red Hat’s Fedora 40 and Fedora Rawhide Linux distributions
Indicators of Compromise: Slow logins via ssh, high CPU usage, and generation of Valgrind errors. The backdoor activates under certain conditions, including systems using the amd64 architecture and running glibc using either Debian- or Red Hat derived distributions. The malicious payload activates if the running program has the process name /usr/sbin/sshd. The RSA_public_decrypt function is redirected into a malicious implementation that can be used to bypass authentication.
